audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.38%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.11%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 è in calo dello 0.41%, il VIX scende dell'1.91%. Il Dollar Index è pressoché invariato. L'oro è in rialzo dello 0.91%, sopra i 4560 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio scende dello 0.81%, sotto i 114 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale americano è in rialzo dell'1.55%, al 4.44%.

L'Australia ha alzato i tassi d'interesse, mossa che contrasta con il trend globale. La Banca Centrale Europea continua a discutere il modello economico europeo, definito 'naif' da alcuni membri.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. La presentazione del rapporto annuale 2025 della BCE all'Europarlamento è prevista, ma non sono attesi annunci di politica monetaria.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra gli ottantamila dollari, con un aumento dell'uno virgola cinque uno percento. I flussi ETF hanno registrato un afflusso netto di circa seicentoventinove milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalla crescente domanda di ETF. Inoltre, alcune notizie positive dall'Iran hanno contribuito al recupero del prezzo.

Per quanto riguarda le altre criptovalute, Ethereum è in aumento dello zero virgola sette uno percento, portandosi a duemilatrecentoottantaquattro dollari. Solana guadagna lo zero virgola uno tre percento, arrivando a ottantaquattro virgola novantasette dollari. BNB invece è pressoché invariato, con una lieve flessione dello zero virgola zero cinque percento.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a cinquanta, nella zona neutrale, suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 0.38%, Shanghai up 0.11%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. The S&P 500 is down 0.41%, the VIX drops 1.91%. The Dollar Index is essentially flat. Gold is up 0.91%, above $4,560 The oil price drops 0.81%, below $114 The 10-year US yield is up 1.55%, at 4.44%. 

The Australian Central Bank raised interest rates, a move that contrasts with the global trend. The European Central Bank continues to discuss the European economic model, described as 'naive' by some members. 

No major macroeconomic data is due today. The presentation of the ECB's 2025 annual report to the European Parliament is scheduled, but no monetary policy announcements are expected.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin holds above eighty thousand dollars, with a 1.51% increase. ETF flows have recorded a net inflow of around $629 million. This movement could be influenced by growing ETF demand. Additionally, some positive news from Iran have contributed to the price recovery. 

Regarding other cryptocurrencies, Ethereum is up 0.71%, reaching $2,384 Solana gains 0.13%, arriving at $84.97 BNB is essentially flat, with a slight decline of 0.05%.

The Fear & Greed Index is at 50, in the neutral zone, suggesting investor caution.

We are awaiting today's economic data releases. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Looking at Europe With a Sharper Eye
articles.snippet: Welcome to The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest of Ukrainian commentary and analysis from across the political spectrum only for War on the Rocks members. Each Monday, we bring you a curated selection of articles from Ukrainian media offering insight into how Ukrainians themselves debate the issues shaping their country.American coverage often narrows the view to the battlefield — these pieces widen it, revealing the texture of daily life, politics, and public argument in a nation at war. The perspectives gathered here are varied, candid, and often surprising, together forming a more complete picture of Ukraine as it really is.Frontline and StrategyЕспресо — The post Looking at Europe With a Sharper Eye appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Cheap Missiles, Not Drones, Will Win the Next Air War
articles.snippet: After four years of watching the war in Ukraine, NATO defense decision-makers are finally beginning to pour money into drones. The Iran conflict has drawn further attention to these investments. The assumption is that unmanned aerial systems will ensure a long-term advantage in conflicts requiring ground operations and infrastructure defense.But the battlefield in Ukraine is already pointing toward a different future. articles.title: How to Win a Trade War: Book launch and discussion with Bown and Keynes
articles.snippet: Please join us online for a discussion with Soumaya Keynes and Chad P. Bown on their new book How to Win a Trade War, available for pre-order. articles.title: The Consensus on China’s Economy Is Strong—and Wrong
articles.snippet: Calling on China to change its globally distortionary development strategy may well be warranted. But critics cannot question Chinese mercantilism on the grounds that it penalizes China's consumers, whose standard of living has risen faster than anywhere else in history.

articles.title: How China Killed Every Rare Earth Competitor Before It Could Get Started
articles.snippet: China’s most effective weapon in the rare earth war wasn’t a missile, a tariff, or a trade embargo. It was a price tag. For more than two decades, Beijing has used a remarkably simple strategy to maintain its stranglehold on the global rare earth supply chain: whenever a Western company would get serious about building an independent processing capability, China would act to crash prices. And the result is generally the same: the investment case falls apart, the funding disappears, and the company folds. China’s monopoly survives…

articles.title: ADNOC Accelerates $55 Billion Investment after UAE’s OPEC Exit
articles.snippet: The Abu Dhabi national oil company, ADNOC, is accelerating investment in growth and production after the United Arab Emirates (UAE) left OPEC on May 1. The state oil and gas firm of what was OPEC’s fourth-largest producer before abruptly quitting last week, plans to award as much as $55 billion (200 billion UAE dirhams) on upstream and downstream projects over the next two years. The announcement of accelerated growth and delivery of the strategy came days after the UAE said it would quit OPEC effective May 1 to pursue its national interests.…
